connections.why: Moles and equations from C1 quantify the changes studied in C2
Bonding and structure underpin the behaviour of carbon compounds
Periodic Table foundations are extended to the p- and d-blocks
Redox in C2 develops into electrode potentials in PI1
Introductory rates are formalised as rate equations in PI3
Thermochemistry extends to entropy and feasibility in PI4
Simple equilibria become quantitative Kc, Kp and Ka in PI5
Electrode potentials explain transition-metal redox chemistry
Free-energy feasibility connects to the position of equilibrium
Basic organic chemistry leads into stereoisomerism and aromaticity
Alcohols and acids from C3 are developed in OA2
Aromaticity and isomerism shape oxygen-containing reactions
Acid derivatives react with amines to form amides and peptides
Aromatic amines extend the chemistry of nitrogen compounds
Functional-group reactions are combined into synthetic routes
Nitrogen chemistry adds steps to multi-stage synthesis
Instrumental analysis introduced in C3 underpins OA4 structure determination
Acid-base equilibria explain the behaviour of amino acids
